@@ -0,0 +1,215 @@ +--- +title: "ADR-040: Template inheritance — `{% extends %}` + named `{% block %}`" +sidebar: + label: ADR-040 extends/block inheritance +--- + +*Status:* **Proposed.** *Date:* 2026-06-11. Applies to the *statement-tag dialects* with a layout +surface — *MaxBars* (the PureScript reference / oracle) and *Trussbars* (the Rust production engine). +*RawBars* is the **desugar target**, not a surface consumer: inheritance lowers *to* its +partial/yield primitives. *ClassicBars* and *MinBars* are **out of scope** — ClassicBars keeps +Handlebars' `{{#> }}` partial-block, MinBars (Mustache) has no inheritance. Picks up the one +capability [ADR-039](/adr/adr-0039-liquid-django-surface-alignment/) explicitly deferred (its +Non-goals: "Django's *named multi-block* template inheritance … is out") and builds directly on the +single-slot layout primitives shipped there — `{% partial "layout" %}…{% endpartial %}` + `{% yield %}` +(ADR-039 item 5) and `{% include "name" %}`. + +## Context + +Trussbars now has the **single-slot** layout pattern: a base template exposes one anonymous hole with +`{% yield %}`, and a caller drives it with `{% partial "base" %}body{% endpartial %}`, dropping its +body into that hole. That is genuine inheritance for the common "one content area inside a chrome" +case, and it is enough for Jekyll-style front-matter layouts. + +It is **not** enough for the template systems that own the server-rendered market — Django, Jinja2, +Tera (Zola), Askama/Rinja, Liquid-with-`{% layout %}`. Every one of them composes pages with +*named, multi-slot* inheritance: + +```django +{# base.html #} +{% block title %}Site{% endblock %} +{% block content %}{% endblock %}{% block footer %}© Acme{% endblock %} + +{# page.html #} +{% extends "base.html" %} +{% block title %}Welcome — {% super %}{% endblock %} +{% block content %}

Hi

{% endblock %} +{# footer not overridden → inherits base's "© Acme" #} +``` + +Three capabilities the single slot lacks: **(1)** more than one hole per layout, addressed **by name** +rather than by position; **(2)** a *default* body per hole that survives when the child does not +override it; **(3)** a way for an override to splice in the **parent's** body (`super`). This is the +deferred generalization, and it is the single biggest gap blocking the northstar ports — mdBook-class +docs themes get by on single-slot, but any Django/Zola/Askama app port stalls here. + +The design tension is that Trussbars is **AOT-compiled, typed, and logic-free in templates** +(StringTemplate model–view separation — no in-template lambdas, no arbitrary runtime logic). So the +inheritance design must (a) resolve **statically** — the `extends` chain and block names known at +compile time — so the AOT backend can flatten it to straight-line Rust with the typed context +inference (docs/03) seeing one merged template; and (b) introduce **no new runtime machinery** beyond +what the partial/yield primitives already provide. + +## Decision + +Add **compile-time, statically-resolved, single-chain named-block inheritance**. Two surface +statements, one structural slot, all desugaring to the existing partial/yield registry — no new engine +primitive, no runtime inheritance object. + +### Surface + +| Form | Role | +| --- | --- | +| `{% extends "base" %}` | This template *refines* `base`. Must be the first non-whitespace node. String-literal name, parsed by the same quoted-name reader as `{% include "name" %}`. | +| `{% block name %}…{% endblock %}` | Declare a named, overridable slot. In a *base*, the body is the **default**. In a *child*, the body is the **override**. `name` is a bare identifier, unique per template. | +| `{% super %}` | Inside a child block, splice in the **parent** block's body at this point. A structural slot, exactly like `{% yield %}`. | + +`{% endblock %}` may name its block for readability — `{% endblock content %}` — and the name, if +present, must match (a located `DisallowedShape` error otherwise, like the `case`-leading rule). + +### Semantics (Django-compatible, statically resolved) + +1. **The chain.** `{% extends "B" %}` makes `B` the parent; `B` may itself `{% extends %}`. The chain + is a list of string-literal names resolved against the partial/inline registry at lower time — the + same registry `hoistInline` ([Kernel.Hoist](/engine/host-api/)) populates. No runtime lookup. +2. **Merge.** The *root* of the chain (the topmost base) supplies the page skeleton. Walking + leaf→root, each `{% block name %}` override replaces the body of the same-named block below it; an + un-overridden block keeps the nearest-ancestor body (its default if never overridden). Block + identity is **by name across the whole chain**, not by lexical nesting. +3. **`{% super %}`** in an override renders the body that block *would have had* one level up the chain + (the parent's override, or the base default). Outside a block, or with no parent block of that + name, it is a located error. +4. **A child is blocks-only.** A template with `{% extends %}` may contain, at top level, **only** + `{% block %}` definitions (and whitespace/comments). Stray content outside a block is a located + `DisallowedShape` error — *not* silently dropped (the no-silent-no-op bar, CLAUDE.md) — with the + fix-it "move this into a `{% block %}`, or remove the `{% extends %}`". (Django silently ignores it; + we reject, consistent with how this project treats every removed/!misused surface form.) +5. **Single inheritance.** One `{% extends %}` per template; a second is a located error. Diamonds + cannot arise (linear chain). A cycle in the chain is a located error caught at lower time. + +### `{% yield %}` and `{% block %}` are duals — and they unify + +`{% yield %}` is the **anonymous, single, defaultless** slot; `{% block name %}default{% endblock %}` +is the **named, multi, defaulted** slot. They are the same mechanism at two ergonomic points, so the +desugar is one target: + +* `{% yield %}` ≡ a block with the reserved anonymous name and an empty default. +* `{% partial "L" %}body{% endpartial %}` ≡ `{% extends "L" %}{% block ⟨anon⟩ %}body{% endblock %}`. + +So the single-slot layout shipped in ADR-039 becomes the **degenerate one-block case** of this ADR — +not a parallel mechanism. The lower pass that already lifts `{% inline %}` definitions and threads the +`{% yield %}` slot is extended to thread *named* slots; nothing new lands in the interpret driver, the +compiler emit driver, or the runtime. + +## The engine model — a lower-phase pre-pass (the IoC `desugar` instance) + +Inheritance is a **structural rewrite**, so it slots into the existing `desugar` IoC instance +(`foldTemplate` + rewrite rules, `Kernel.Lower`) and runs as a pre-pass beside `hoistInline` +(propose: `Kernel.Inherit.resolveInheritance`). Given the parsed skeleton + the partial registry: + +1. If the template has no `{% extends %}`, collect its `{% block %}` bodies as the slot defaults and + leave it otherwise untouched (a base *is* a renderable template). +2. If it extends `B`, resolve `B` from the registry, recurse to flatten `B`, then overlay this + template's blocks (rule 2) and resolve every `{% super %}` against the pre-overlay body. The result + is **one flattened skeleton** with all blocks inlined — a plain template the existing interpret / + compile / validate drivers consume unchanged. + +Because the flatten is total and static, three properties fall out for free: + +* **AOT (Trussbars).** The flattened skeleton is what the Rust backend lowers — inheritance costs + **zero runtime**; it is gone before codegen. Schema inference (docs/03) infers the typed context of + the *merged* page in one pass. This is the differentiator: Django/Tera/Jinja resolve inheritance per + request at runtime; Trussbars resolves it at compile time, the way Askama does — but with the + Django/Liquid surface. +* **VM (Trussbars dynamic).** The same flatten runs once at template-load; the VM executes the merged + program. AOT≡VM parity (the conformance invariant) holds because both consume the identical + flattened skeleton. +* **Source maps / Context Inspector (ADR-035).** Provenance is preserved by carrying each inlined + block's original span through the overlay, so a value in the rendered page still maps to the + `{% block %}` (base *or* child) it came from. + +### Why `{% super %}`, not `{{ block.super }}` / `{{ super() }}` + +Django spells the parent splice `{{ block.super }}`, Jinja `{{ super() }}`. Both are **rejected**: in +the statement-tag dialects `{{ }}` is **output-only** (ADR-039 Tier 1 invariant) — it carries *data*, +never control or structure, and there are no in-template calls (`super()` is a call; `block.super` is a +magic path). A structural splice is a *statement*. `{% yield %}` already set this precedent (the +hyphen-free, sigil-free spelling of a structural slot — ADR-039 item 5), and `{% super %}` is its exact +sibling: the slot that pulls the *parent's* body the way `{% yield %}` pulls the *caller's*. One rule — +structure is `{% %}`, output is `{{ }}` — stays intact. + +## Consequences + +### Migration & blast radius + +**Additive — zero existing-corpus migration.** Inheritance is a *new* surface; nothing that parses +today changes meaning. The single-slot `{% partial %}`/`{% yield %}` forms keep working verbatim (they +become the degenerate case but are not rewritten). The only corpus churn is *new* golden cases +exercising multi-block chains. Contrast ADR-039 item 6 (the `and`/`or`/`not` cutover) whose blast +radius spanned every boolean expression — this one has none. + +### Gates + +* **Conformance (`trussbars/conformance/harness.mjs`).** Add multi-block-chain cases; the oracle + (PureScript `renderMaxbars`), AOT (`compileMaxRust`), and VM must stay byte-identical across all four + modes (`--v2`/`--vm`/`--vm-compat`/`--compat-parity`). The flatten runs in the shared lower pass, so + AOT≡VM≡oracle is structural, not per-backend. +* **`test:compile`** (interpreter ≡ compiled JS) gains the same cases — the JS runtime consumes the + flattened skeleton, so no `flatbars-runtime.mjs` change is expected. +* **`check:parity`** (RawBars ≡ MaxBars): RawBars is the desugar target, so a flattened MaxBars + inheritance program must equal the hand-written RawBars partial/yield program it lowers to. +* **Strict rejects** (new `DisallowedShape` cases, pinned like `check:dialect-diagnostics`): a child + with stray top-level content; a duplicate block name; a second `{% extends %}`; a mismatched + `{% endblock name %}`; `{% super %}` outside a block / with no parent; an `{% extends %}` cycle or + unknown base. Each located, each with a fix-it. +* **Editors** (ADR-017): `extends`/`block`/`endblock`/`super` join the operation vocabulary + (`editors/operations.json` + `token-vocabulary.json`) so highlighting, hover, and folding cover them; + `check:operations-paint` extends to the new heads. + +### Documentation + +* `engine/maxbars.mdx` — promote the existing "block-partial body (`{% yield %}`)" section to a + "Layouts & inheritance" section presenting the `{% yield %}` → `{% block %}` continuum. +* The `/maxbars` tutorial gains a multi-block inheritance example (gate-validated by + `check:tutorial-links`). +* `trussbars/docs/` — a new feature doc; mark the relevant docs/19 / docs/06-freeze tail item. +* The helper/operation catalog regenerates (`gen:catalog`, `gen:operations`) for the new heads. + +## Design invariants — the ceiling this stays under + +1. **Static resolution only.** Every `extends` target and `block` name is known at compile time (string + literals / bare identifiers — no computed `{% extends someVar %}`). This is what keeps AOT codegen + and typed-context inference possible; a dynamic parent is **out** by construction, not omission. +2. **No new runtime, no new engine primitive.** Inheritance is a lower-phase flatten to the + partial/yield registry. The interpret driver, compiler emit driver, and runtime are untouched. +3. **`{{ }}` stays output-only.** The parent splice is `{% super %}`, never `{{ super() }}` / + `{{ block.super }}`. Structure is `{% %}`; output is data. +4. **No silent no-ops.** Every misuse (stray child content, dup/mismatched/duplicate block, double + extends, orphan `super`, unknown/cyclic base) is a *located, actionable* error — never silently + dropped the way Django drops stray content. +5. **Single linear chain.** One `{% extends %}` per template; no multiple inheritance, no mixins. + +## Non-goals (deliberately deferred) + +* **Dynamic / computed parents** (`{% extends some_expr %}`). Breaks static resolution (invariant 1). + Django allows it; we do not — and the typed AOT story is the reason. +* **Block-scoped `{% block name scoped %}`** (Jinja's loop-variable capture into a block). The + flattened-skeleton model already shares the enclosing scope; the explicit `scoped` modifier is a + finer-grained capture we can add later if a port needs it. +* **`{{ block.super }}` as a *value*** (passing the parent body around as data). `{% super %}` is a + structural splice, not an expression — consistent with `{% yield %}` never being a value. +* **Mixins / multiple inheritance / `{% use %}`-style horizontal composition.** Single linear chain + only (invariant 5). Horizontal reuse is what `{% include %}` is for. +* **Cross-dialect surface in ClassicBars/MinBars.** ClassicBars keeps Handlebars `{{#> }}`; MinBars has + no inheritance. The *mechanism* lives in the shared kernel; only the statement-tag surface is added. + +## Open question + +**The anonymous-block spelling for the `{% yield %}` unification.** The desugar treats `{% yield %}` as +a block with a reserved anonymous name (so `{% partial %}` and `{% extends %}` share one flatten). That +reserved name must be one a user can never write as a `{% block %}` identifier. Options: a sentinel that +fails the bare-identifier lexer (e.g. an internal `@yield` key never surface-reachable), or keep +`{% yield %}` a genuinely *separate* anonymous slot in the lower pass and only *share the overlay +logic*. The second is less elegant but sidesteps the reserved-name question entirely — decide at +implementation, in the ADR's spirit of "settle the surface on paper, allow one internal seam to be +chosen in code."
